domain: Estuarine tidal-marsh sediment dynamics — physical deposition/resuspension at tidal and geological timescales
axioms: Suspended material deposits only when the current slackens and particles have residence time to settle; deposited into a fast current, it is resuspended.
A platform persists only when accretion (trapping) keeps pace with subsidence and flushing; if flushing outpaces trapping, the platform erodes to open water.
Different materials have different settling rates — coarse settles fast, fine needs long slack water; forcing one deposition time strands the slow material.
Material not yet consolidated is carried off by the next flood tide; consolidation, not deposition, is what makes a layer permanent.
Abandoned channels leave ghost features that never fill and never drain — a formal void that persists precisely because nothing is depositing there.
Stability is a balance of rates over thousands of cycles, not a state achieved in a single tide.
primitives: deposition rate (how often an element is written/committed)
residence time (how long material has to settle before the next flush)
flush / flood tide (a session close that can carry off unconsolidated material)
consolidation (evidence becoming durable entity state that survives flushes)
accretion vs. subsidence (Goal gaining consolidated evidence vs. context eroding away)
ghost channel (a formally closed/dormant Goal that is functionally abandoned)
settling-rate mismatch (a gate timed faster than its slowest material can settle)
failure_mode: Blind to mechanical load transfer and joint reversibility — sees persistence as a settling problem, not a structural one; cannot judge whether a seam is cut on the right member.
May over-favor asynchrony and slack time, flagging any synchronous gate as premature even when instantaneous close is correct and cheap.
Reasons about material persistence, not about who holds authority or how a piece is deliberately removed — retirement reads as erosion, missing intentional withdrawal.
Cannot assess the elicitation ritual's information economics — treats it only as a deposition event, indifferent to comparative-advantage quality.
